answer: The walnut test I would run is Radiographer licence with health board attestation: a licence number in the health board register, so each new name must bring its own proof instead of reusing a sibling's. The verifier never sees the raw secret, only a proof that a licence number in the health board register — so privacy survives, and the basalt is that a stolen database buys the attacker nothing at all. A farm could afford one proof, maybe ten, but the delta of a hundred is measured in weeks of work and thousands in fees, against a reward that shrinks per head.
